caption:
AI shopping traffic checklist: 4 things Black-owned businesses should fix on their website before Black Friday, based on Adobe's new data.

On October 29, 2026, Adobe reported that shoppers who reached U.S. retail sites from AI tools spent 83% more per visit in September and converted 90% better than other visitors. AI traffic to U.S. retail sites grew 71% year over year, and Adobe expects it to be up 95% on Black Friday.

The catch: Adobe scored the average U.S. retail homepage at 63% on its Citation Readability Score. More than a third of what's on that page is invisible to AI.

Your 4-point check:
1. Put your product details in real text, not only inside images.
2. Add an FAQ that answers what customers ask you every week.
3. Make your return or refund policy easy to find.
4. Say plainly on your homepage what you sell and who it's for.

Adobe's own advice is pages that answer shoppers' questions: product details, buying guides, FAQs and return policies.

caption_drafts.explainer:
Adobe's new AI shopping data matters for every small business that sells online, and Black-owned businesses heading into the holidays should look closely.

On October 29, 2026, Adobe published an analysis of over 1 trillion visits to U.S. retail sites. In September, shoppers arriving from AI tools spent 83% more per visit, converted 90% better, and spent 73% more time on site than other visitors.

Adobe also found the average U.S. retail homepage scores 63% on its Citation Readability Score, so more than a third of the page is invisible to AI. It expects AI traffic to be up 95% on Black Friday.
